data.one_liner: Integrate Apple Pay on iOS and Google Pay on Android with ready-made buttons.
data.what_it_does: Provides unified Flutter support for Apple Pay and Google Pay. It includes prebuilt, guideline-compliant payment buttons as well as lower-level client APIs to verify payment availability and request payment tokens. The resulting payment tokens can then be passed to a backend or payment processor.
use_when: You want to offer Apple Pay on iOS and Google Pay on Android for digital or physical purchases.
You need standard branded Google Pay and Apple Pay button widgets that handle user payment triggers.
You want a client-side wrapper to obtain payment tokens without implementing native PassKit or Google Pay SDKs manually.
avoid_when: Selling digital goods governed by Google Play or App Store In-App Purchase policies (use in_app_purchase instead).
Targeting platforms other than Android and iOS, such as web or desktop.
You want an all-in-one payment processing solution that directly charges cards without a separate payment gateway.
strengths: Official style and guideline compliance for Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons.
Provides both easy prebuilt widgets (GooglePayButton, ApplePayButton) and low-level imperative client control (Pay).
Supports loading configuration profiles directly from JSON strings or asset files.
weaknesses: Requires substantial merchant and certificate configuration outside Flutter with Apple and Google.
Advanced Android integrations require manual EventChannel setup to handle lifecycle recreation results.
Does not process the transaction itself; only obtains payment tokens that must be sent to your PSP.
data.setup_notes: Requires setting up Apple Developer merchant IDs and payment processing certificates for Apple Pay, and signing up for the Google Pay Business Console with integration approval for Android.

alternatives.name: flutter_stripe
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick if you want a complete Stripe processing pipeline including cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay in one SDK.
